Write a TOC snapshot

Source: R/toc.R
toc_write.Rd

Writes a canonical TOC table to a file. Use it to dump a live database TOC for offline work, to version-control title metadata, or to hand it to another language.

Usage

toc_write(
  toc,
  path,
  source = or_default(attr(toc, "toc_meta")$source, "tlfstack"),
  schema = toc_schema()
)

Arguments

toc

A canonical TOC table (from toc_read()) or a data frame in the layout described by schema.

path

Output file. The format is taken from the extension: .json, .yml, .yaml or .csv.

source

Text recorded in the source header field.

schema

A toc_schema(). It is used to normalize a flat toc, and for the CSV column names and delimiter.

Value

path, invisibly.

Details

The JSON and YAML formats share one structure:

tlfstack_toc: 1                 # format version
generated_at: 2026-10-22T09:00:00+0000
source: database                # where the snapshot came from
outputs:
  - program: t_demo
    scope: {study: STUDY01}
    type: Table
    number: "14.1.1"
    title: [Summary of Demographic and Baseline Characteristics]
    subtitle: [Safety Population]
    footnotes: [Percentages are based on N in each column.]
    output_file_name: t-14-01-01-demog.rtf

Multi-line fields are arrays, so no delimiter convention is needed and output numbers stay strings. A JSON Schema for the format ships with the package: system.file("schema", "tlfstack-toc-v1.schema.json", package = "tlfstack"). CSV output joins multi-line fields with the schema delimiter, for tools that need a flat file.

Examples

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
toc_write(ex_toc, f, source = "example")
identical(toc_read(toc_source_file(f))$number, ex_toc$number)
#> [1] TRUE
unlink(f)
